- Phase 4, addendum 002 (status rhythm), how it is applied. Config: `status.maxGapMinutes`, `status.minGapMinutes`, `status.maxPictures` and `status.inlineMaxTries` are in `config/showcase.json`, are required by the startup validation in `src/config.ts`, and are read from there by the harness. Looks: `tools/lib/looks.ts` logs every still, sheet, crop page and comparison the harness writes (the hook is `writeRecord`, so no command can forget it) as a JPEG copy with a caption under `out/work/looks/`, newest 96 kept; frames of a sheet or a sequence are logged at most every 45 s. Long jobs: every render through `openSource` (film, clip, pack, measure, stress, budget) writes a look of the frame it is on when it starts and then every `min(status.minGapMinutes, status.maxGapMinutes / 2)` minutes, taken from the pixels it already grabbed or from the canvas, never by rendering again. `npm run status` no longer renders: it shows, per stop, the newest key frame beside the approved image (a comparison, or the newest hold or terrain frame set beside the approved image), then the newest other looks; with no stop the newest looks since the last status, then the kept whole film sheets; it never returns empty. `--render` keeps the old behavior of addendum 001 (both comparisons and a dive sheet at the review tier). It writes the pictures to `out/stills/status/`, the packed file for the inline grid, one line into the Session log, the review page from the build as it stands (`tools/review.ts --no-build`), and with `--push` commits and pushes. `npm run status -- --due` says how long ago the last status was; it is asked at every poll. Supporting agents: `npm run looks -- --push --folder ID` writes the newest eight looks as one commit to the branch `agent/ID-looks` with git plumbing (the agent's own branch and working tree are not touched); `npm run looks -- --fetch` reads every such branch into `out/work/looks/remote/` without merging; `npm run looks -- --add FILE --label TEXT` logs any picture an agent is looking at (a painted map, a fit overlay). With eight stops in work at once and four pictures per status, each status shows the stops with the newest looks and names the others in its text.
- Phase 4, one change to the shared engine before the eight stops start, so that a plan change at one stop no longer needs a shared file written again. Before: `src/space/skyframe.json` stored the sky frame, the terrain sky turn and the patch aims as numbers that followed from the plans of every stop up to Mars, a test failed whenever a plan moved, and a tool wrote them again. With eight agents changing eight plans at once that file would conflict at every merge and change the engine hash each time. Now `FilmDirector` computes the same values from the stored arguments and the plans when it starts (`aimSky()` in `src/director/film.ts`, the aim math moved to `src/space/aim.ts`), rounded to seven decimals exactly as the tool rounded them; `skyframe.json` keeps only the arguments, the grade, the band, the stars and the two patch aims of the stop the sky is fitted to (they do not depend on any plan). New for the other stops: every stop gets an orbit patch aim on the view of its judged hold frame, a terrain patch aim on the view of its judged terrain frame, and may ask for a sky turn in its terrain view with `skyAim.terrain` in its `plan.ts` (band position, tilt and lift in degrees, as Mars uses). The engine sets each sky patch's aim from these when it draws. Checked: the computed frame, turn and both Mars patch aims equal the stored numbers digit for digit (`out/work/an` check, values in the commit), tests 24 green.
- Phase 4, how the eight stops are built. One supporting agent per stop, each on its own VM, all eight at once, in the order of `buildOrderAfterLookLock` when it comes to rounds, finishing and publishing. Each agent owns `src/stops/<id>/`, `public/assets/<id>/` and `assets-src/<id>/`, pushes to `agent/<id>`, pushes its newest looks to `agent/<id>-looks` at least every `status.maxGapMinutes`, and keeps its own notebook in `assets-src/<id>/NOTES.md`. Their standing instructions are `assets-src/shared/STOP-AGENT.md`, in the repo so an agent can read them again after a compaction. What a stop needs beyond the shared modules (rings, cloud layers, plasma loops) lives in the stop's own folder, so it is hashed with the stop and cannot change another stop. A change that only the shared engine can carry arrives as `assets-src/<id>/engine.patch` with a note; the Builder applies it to `main` only if it is additive and off by default, and checks Mars frame 2325 and frame 2580 byte for byte after it. The Builder integrates each stop with `git checkout origin/agent/<id> -- <its three folders>`, never by merging the branch, then runs the machine checks, the measures, the pack and the critics, and sends the issues back to the stop's agent. Disk budgets given to the agents: 150 MB for a stop's `full` set and 40 MB for its `web` set, so nine stops stay inside `repo.maxTreeGb` and the published site inside its 500 MB.

Setup proof: each rendered Mars frame 2325 at the draft tier and reported the first 16 characters of its sha256, `fd128b1a999f76fa`, the same as the Builder's VM (one worker mistyped it once and corrected it; its first job is compared byte by byte here like every other). More workers are started for the sandbox master in Phase 6.

- Phase 4, the sky aim per stop (decided 04:45 UTC on 2026-11-21, on main with engine batch 3). The hazard: each stop's world rotation follows from the stop before it (`place()` in `src/director/film.ts` turns a stop about the one Sun direction by an angle that comes from the previous stop's `travel.turnDeg` and `side` and from its exit pose), and the one sky is anchored to the Mars hold. So a plan change at one stop moved the fixed sky behind every stop after it, and a sky patch whose rim was matched to the sky around it would no longer match. With eight agents changing eight plans at once that would happen at every merge. The rule that stays: `kit/03-METHOD.md` section 5, "The sky keeps one orientation for the whole film. It turns only because the camera turns.", applied with the Phase 3 precedent that the sky may change its turn only under a cover, where no frame shows it (Mars's terrain sky does this since round 4). Built: an optional `skyAim: { orbit: [along, tilt, lift] }` in a stop's plan, the sky direction and roll the camera sees at the judged `hold` frame. A stop's aim holds from the rise of the stop before it (after that rise's cover), through that travel and its own hold, to its own dive cover; the terrain view uses `skyAim.terrain` or keeps the orbit turn; a stop's rise (orbit side) and travel already carry the next stop's turn; the ending keeps Neptune's. Three special cases: Jupiter's orbit aim is ignored, because its arrival shares the sky with the approved Mars rise, so Jupiter's sky follows only from Mars and its own plan; the Sun's hold shares its sky with Mercury's arrival (no cover lies between), so Mercury's aim decides and the Sun's is used only while Mercury has none; a stop without an aim carries the turn of the stop before it. With no aim declared nothing changes, which the byte check of batch 3 shows. `npm run -s aim [-- --stop ID]` (`tools/aim.ts`) prints each stop's present aims as the line to paste and what its plan sets. Tested here at the draft tier: pasting the printed aim leaves the hold frame pixel identical; a Jupiter aim is ignored; a Saturn aim changes the Saturn hold and the Jupiter rise frame 3296 and nothing else. A first variant that blended the turn during the travel passed its byte check and was dropped, because it turned the sky in view. Told to the stop agents in `assets-src/shared/STOP-AGENT.md`, section "Sky aim".

One change, the Uranus agent's engine request 1 (`assets-src/uranus/ENGINE-REQUESTS.md` on `agent/uranus` fd27cc1): in `Sky.render` the ray of the sky pass is built from the inverse projection and divided by the float32 sum of two of its terms; low over a planet (near plane 0.02 of the altitude, far plane 80000) the two terms are 250 to 1250 and on some frames cancel to exactly 0, so the whole sky pass (band, patches, Sun disc and corona) drops out for that one frame while the stars stay. The agent listed the frames hit in mercury, venus, earth, mars (2453, 2700, 2702), jupiter, uranus and neptune; it is the cause of "the Milky Way pops on between 4415 and 4416" in the Uranus scorecard. The fix: when that float32 sum is exactly 0 the two terms are set to 0 and 1, which gives the true ray; every other frame takes the old path with the old numbers. An order mistake of mine, logged as it happened: the batch went to main with the push of Status 22 at 11:12 (the status tool pushes the checked out branch, and I had not switched back to `main`) before the byte check had come back. - Phase 4, which build of a stop is kept at the round limit (14:57 UTC on 2026-11-21, written before any third round is scored). `kit/07-QUALITY-BAR.md`: "When a loop reaches its limit without passing: keep the best build of that stop". The builds of a stop are the ones judged in its rounds, each at its judged commit. They are ranked in this order: (1) machine checks and measures green before not green; (2) the distance from the pass bar, the sum over R1, R3 and R4 of how far each score is under `quality.passScore`, smaller first; (3) the higher R4, by Brandon's order to put the motion first; (4) fewer severe issues; (5) fewer major issues, a failed R2 counted as one, as the kit counts it; (6) the later round. The Builder looks at the judged frames and the sheets of the two best builds side by side before keeping one, and writes here if what is seen contradicts the ranking; the ranking decides unless a fault the critics did not see is found. When an earlier build wins, the stop's own folders (`src/stops/<id>/`, `public/assets/<id>/`, `assets-src/<id>/`) are taken from that round's judged commit onto the current engine, its judged stills are rendered again and looked at beside the round's own (the kit's "Freshness"), and the Stops table carries that round's scores. The open items of a stop are the ones of the kept build's round.

Finding: Earth frame 1870 moves 18.9 px during the shutter and is drawn with 16 samples, a step near 1.2 px, yet it reads as a comb of sharp dashes. Cause: each sample is drawn with the texture detail of a still frame, so thin bright lines stay one pixel sharp in every sample and the sum is a row of lines. Frames at the sample cap (Earth 1875 to 1879) step 2 to 4 px, and a translucent cover (Uranus 4159 to 4161) lowers the sample count although the picture still shows through. Rung 2 (blur along the motion inside a sample) is held back: it needs a velocity pass and costs every frame. Given to engine_profiler on agent/engine-perf; merged only after the Mars byte proof.

Overload resolution failed`. Cause: the page lost its drawing context in the middle of the job (software drawing under memory pressure), the browser restored it, and the engine could not upload its textures again because `src/core/sets.ts` frees each decoded image after the first upload; every frame after that is black and the tool still wrote it. The Builder's own sheet of the same segment on the same commit has no such line and twelve good frames, so the frames themselves are sound. Decision: (1) capture side, now: `tools/lib/browser.ts` counts lost contexts and reads the page's console for the upload and shader errors, `renderPng` throws on either, and stills and sheets render the frame again on a fresh page (up to 3 tries); the film render stops with exit code 3 and is resumed by running the same command again. Proved by forcing a context loss in a test: the old symptom appeared (18 upload errors), the guard threw, the fresh page drew the frame. `npx tsc --noEmit` and 62 tests pass, the engine hash is unchanged (f854c8146f64c7e4), so open rounds and records stay valid. (2) Engine side, with batch 16: the app frees and loads its sets again when the context is restored, so the live app does not go black either. (3) The broken sheet is not shown to critics; the segment is rendered again on two workers and the Builder looks at every tile before the pack. Every sheet and every clip is checked for black frames before it is used.

- Phase 5 step 4, the sky grade: one band look for the film (decided 00:55 UTC on 2026-11-22). `kit/03-METHOD.md` section 5 asks for one sky "graded to match the approved images", and R5 asks "one grade, one lens, one sky". Measured by eye on the montage of the 18 approved images: the band is warm grey brown to gold with dark dust in seven of them (strongest at Uranus, Jupiter and Venus), cool grey blue only at Mars, and Saturn's sky is plain. The shared band was graded against Mars in Phase 3, which is why it is blue violet with olive haze, and the travel agent's fourth task graded the flight band gold and tied that grade to the flight lift, so the colour follows the exposure. Decision: (a) colour and exposure are separated: the flight lift changes brightness only; (b) the band's look becomes a weight per stop between today's shared look (0) and the warm flight grade (1), held for every segment of the stop, and in a travel it moves from the leaving stop's weight to the arriving stop's together with the arriving sky patch, slowly and only once; the ending keeps Neptune's weight, so the retreat and the lookback show one band; (c) the engine change lands with every weight at 0, so every stop frame stays the same bytes and the proof stays a byte proof; (d) the weights are then set to 1 for every stop but Mars in one commit of their own (Mars stays at 0: it is approved and its frames stay the same bytes), and every finished stop's judged stills are rendered again and looked at beside the kept ones as Freshness asks, the rise frames too, since that is where the shared band shows (Saturn 3866, Uranus 4436, Earth 2156). If a stop looks worse with the warm band its weight goes back to 0 and the travels on both sides carry the change. (e) The arriving sky patch comes in over at least twenty frames and the band is not switched off where Saturn's plain sky comes in: the patch fades in while the lift closes. This is the travel agent's sixth task, with the judged travel frames (the next body as a point of light and the band or a dense field in frame at 1642, 3922 and 4492).

- Phase 5, the cause of frames that do not repeat (03:10 UTC on 2026-11-22). The Saturn agent found it on its own stop (`agent/saturn` 7dc2542, notes in `assets-src/saturn/NOTES.md` under "Item 8"): the harness GPU shades 2 x 2 pixel quads; a pixel that hit `discard` stops storing to variables, so a local first assigned after the discard holds stale memory, and `dFdx`, `dFdy`, `fwidth` and `texture()` without an explicit level read it for the live neighbours of the quad. Its haze shell began with a discard and later took `dFdx` inside the ring shadow. After its fix (no discard before the last statement, no cross pixel operation on a value first assigned in a per pixel branch) 3866, 3594, 3567 and 3840 gave one hash each in 11 renders over 3 fresh sessions, where 3866 gave 6 hashes in 12 renders before. What the Builder did with it: the engine agent's task 5 became an audit of every fragment shader for the pattern, shared code first, with a fix on `agent/engine-batch19` and a list per stop folder (MAIL 62); every stop agent got the rule for its own shaders with its next commit (MAIL 63, with the news that batch 18 is on main). G3 as the kit defines it (the first hold, dive, travel and terrain segment, fresh loads and reversed order) is green on main and does not sample the frames in question, so no machine check is red; the fix reaches main with Saturn's polish in Phase 6 and with batch 19 for shared code. - Arrivals, decided 08:47 UTC on 2026-11-22 after looking at both patterns on earth.travel at draft: the arriving body is pinned on screen. - 05:27 UTC why the chain stopped at the preview film at 01:38 UTC, and the fix, which is in `tools/` only and changes no pixel. Finding: `npm run film -- --format preview --from-master` made a film of 5401 frames from a master of 5400 and refused it, rightly. The master's frame times were even (5400 packets, each 512 ticks after the last, 180.000 s), but its decode times were not: spans that x264 wrote with reordered frames (a delay of two frames) are joined without encoding to spans it wrote without any (spans of two frames), and at such a seam the mp4 holds a packet three frames long followed by packets one tick long; the join of 05:28 UTC counts the packets it had to give a new decode time or length: 229 in the film, all of them inside the clips (Mercury 22, Venus 67, Earth 46, Jupiter 57, Uranus 16, Neptune 21; none in the clips of the Sun, Mars and Saturn). A player shows every frame at its right time, so nothing was visible in the files as they were, but a converter that reads packet lengths at a constant rate repeats a frame at each seam and drops frames after it: measured on the old clips of Mercury, Jupiter and Neptune, a constant rate decode gave 496 frames for 495 with 346 frames out of place. That is what made the preview one frame long, and it is what a platform could do to a post when it encodes it again, at the very seam between the hold and the dive. Fix: `regularTiming` in `tools/lib/encode.ts`, called by every join without encoding (`concatCopy` for chunks, the film and the clips; `tools/post.ts` for a post). It reads the packet table, requires even frame times, and if a decode time or a packet length is uneven it writes the same stream once more with the same frame times and even decode times (one reorder delay for the whole file), then checks the result and throws if a frame time moved. No picture is encoded again. Proof on Mercury, Jupiter and Neptune: every decoded frame has the same hash before and after (495 of 495), the files differ by about 200 bytes of table, and a constant rate decode of the new file gives the same 495 frames in the same order. The first try (a pass through switch for the scaler) was refused by ffmpeg and dropped; a filter in the scaler alone was weighed and not chosen, because it would have left the clips and the posts as they were. The film and the nine clips are joined again from the same chunks, the film's every frame is compared by hash against the first join, and the eight posts made early are joined again by `npm run post`, as addendum 003 says for a clip that is remade. No intro is made again. The record of a joined file now carries `timing`.

Everything finer comes from functions at the scale of the pixel, and motion comes from the camera, with at most a slow turning carried by fine detail from functions. A deck with no field from the image is as welcome if it is as rich. Reason: plain noise bands would answer the note and fail the bar, and the bar is not lowered.

Measured: the first critics of rounds 37 and 40 score the judged dive and rise frames as smear (Earth 1857 "extreme radial zoom blur and low resolution stretching, blocky stepped streaks", severe; Earth 2156 "dragged into parallel streaks and do not hold detail at native size", severe; Mercury 1016 "smeared into long directional streaks", severe; Mercury 717 major), and the handover reports give the raw shutter motion at those frames as 29, 25, 77 and 59 px at the point that moves most, 25 to 80 px through most of every dive and rise. Cause: one steady move over a factor of about a hundred in 90 frames changes scale by 6 to 14 percent a frame, so the full shutter of `film.shutterDegrees` draws every small bright thing toward the frame edge as a flat ended dash; the path cannot be slower inside the timeline. Brandon's note names the blur first, so the place has to stay sharp on the way down. Decided: in a dive or rise of a stop that opted in, the shutter of a frame is shortened so the motion across it is at most `handover.maxBlurPx` at the point that moves most (start value 6), keeping the middle of the shutter, eased back to the full shutter over the last `handover.blurEaseFrames` of a rise so the travel after it meets no step. `film.shutterDegrees` and every frame outside those segments stay as they are; proof asked for at the review tier. Not a threshold of any check, no rubric and no judged frame changes. Known cost, not measured: with little blur the frame edges move 60 to 150 px from one frame to the next and may strobe in the video; the centre, where the place is, moves a few px. If Brandon sees strobing, the cap is one number in the config. The change goes onto main after rounds 38 and 39 are packed, before round 2 of any stop is judged.

- 2026-11-23 20:27 UTC, d140: the shutter inside a dive and a rise (E6) is set: `handover.maxBlurPx` 14 with `handover.minShutter` 0.5. In words: while the fastest point of the frame moves less than 14 px across the open shutter the shutter is whole (180 degrees, as everywhere else in the film); above that it closes so that the blur stays at 14 px, but never to less than half (90 degrees), so in the fastest frames the blur is half of what the whole shutter gives. Why not the whole shutter: on sharp ground it smears the picture where the dive is fastest (Earth 1882 at the review tier: the clouds at the lower right are streaks and the middle is soft; by the engineer's numbers Mars 2440 has 51 px at the middle of the right edge and 147 px at the corner), and that is the fault Brandon named first in his note ("it's a blurry mess"); the note outranks the kit where the two disagree. Why not a limit alone: the frames are sharp but lie far apart (at Mars 2430 three separate copies in a mean of three frames), which the motion critics of rounds 37 to 40 marked as major (Uranus 4126 to 4175) and which `kit/05-ARCHITECTURE.md` forbids ("Fast motion must come out as a smooth blur"). Why 0.5 and not 0.25: at 0.25 the streak is one eighth of the path between two frames (about 20 px of 160 at the rim of the Mars rise), the staccato of a 45 degree shutter; at 0.5 it is a quarter, the 90 degree shutter that film uses for fast action, with no separate copies (by the engineer's numbers 123 samples at Mars 2440 at the review and at the final tier, and 1.3 px in the middle of the frame). Seen by the Builder: Mars 2440 on main under five shutters (no difference to speak of, because the ground there is the soft globe map: the softness before the surface comes in is the map, and its cure is the place plates of each stop, not the shutter), Earth 1882 under four (the difference is plain), and the engineer's sheets of the Mars rise 2691 to 2693 at floor 0.25 and 0.5 on the eighth bake of the plates (the place stays sharp in the middle at both, and T cannot be named by the blur). This departs from `film.shutterDegrees` inside the dives and rises of stops that hand over and nowhere else: holds, terrain, travel and the ending keep the whole shutter, and the draft tier (one sample at the middle of the shutter) is untouched. Before it goes onto main the tree `builder/e6-on-main-42b1-c14-f50` 3004feba (main 42b1585c with the 21 engine files of `agent/engine-handover` aef36681 and the two numbers) must give the bytes of main on the 115 draft reference frames, on the 18 judged stills at the final tier, and on the 69 frames of the engineer's list at the review tier (the first and last frame of every hold, terrain, travel and ending segment, and frames of dives and rises that keep the whole shutter); those jobs are out (e6p, r69e, r69m). The number is one config key, so a round that shows the half shutter wrong on a stop can change it without an engine change.

Tried: a different arrival for each stop (side, swing, turn angle, turn length, and an off-center start that drifts to the hero framing). Not changed: the hold framing, which is the approved hero image, and the segment times, which are Brandon's in `config/showcase.json`. Next: per stop in Phases 3 and 4, vary what moves inside the hold (orbit direction and amount, moon paths, how far the push goes) and give each dive and rise its own line. If Brandon wants uneven stop lengths, that is a config change through an addendum.

16. Export proof, last frame, found 08:34 UTC on 2026-11-21 at the start of rounds 6 to 10. The proof of Phase 2 was made with the stand-in Sun, so G6, which compares the proof's first frame with a fresh still, went red (13.8 dB) as soon as the real Sun was on main: the gate compared two different films. The proof was made again on this build (`npm run proof`): frame 0, the key frame, 30.53 dB against its still, so G6 is green again; frame 29 is 25.38 dB, under the proof tool's own 30. Side by side the two frames show the same picture, the export one softer: the page's H.264 encoder at `previewFilm.bitrateMbps` (2) cannot hold the Sun's granulation in a predicted frame. No bar is changed. `tools/round.py` now makes the proof again before the gate whenever the engine or the stop that owns frame 0 has changed, so G6 always compares like with like. To settle before the Phase 6 proof (G9 and gauntlet item 15 ask that the proof exists from the final build and that `ffprobe` accepts it; neither asks for the last frame's PSNR, but the tool reports it as a failure and that is not hidden): either the Sun's first second holds 30 dB once its look is final, or the engine's export at the preview size gets the bitrate it needs from a config number, taken with an engine batch and a byte check, never by lowering 30.

The darkest, emptiest area is the starfield, which fills the top 40% of the frame" Tried. Rounds 30 to 31 (batch 20): a pulse of light running along the arch. Rounds 31 to 32 (batch 21, take 2): the loop erupts from the left foot, crosses the crest and lands in the right foot, swells by about a fifth and stays lit to frame 60 (lit pixels in the arch box three times those of frame 0), with the camera pushing in. Frame 0 kept its bytes each time: it is the poster frame, fitted to the approved close image, and it passed its stop; so the arch's share of frame 0 is held. Next, Phase 6, take 3 (MAIL 147 job 1): the arch rising in height and changing its silhouette, one flash that lights the granulation under it, a clearly stronger push toward the sunspot, and no plateau from frame 38 to 60; frame 0 unchanged. Judged again by R6.

Round 30 (job sv31): three exports encoded again at `quality.compressionStressMbps` (the export as it is, a near lossless one, one with stronger detail keeping): the loss is made by the stress encode itself and no export setting moves it. Not done and not to be done: a gentler stress encode, since the test is the kit's. The faintest stars are left as they are: lifting them to pass the encode would change every sky in the film.

174. saturn, `saturn.hold 3465` and `saturn.terrain 3720`, R2, record round 36, fail (counts as one major), items 44 and 108 again: the judged hold and terrain frames drew 0 of 10 votes for "film or game cinematic" (hold b b e b b, terrain b b e b b) against 5 of 10 for the approved images in the stop's own control votes, collected once in round 13 (hold b a e a b, terrain a a e a b). The limit is a gap of 0.2, so 3 of 10 would pass. The same two frames from the same build of the stop (stop hash 47a787cd7f78408c in rounds 35 and 36) drew 3 of 10 from the jurors of round 35 and passed there; rounds 26 and 33 drew 2 and 1 of 10 and failed. The same two approved images drew 2 of 10 when the whole film rounds collected them once more in round 30, and against that the frames would pass; the kit reuses a stop's own collection, so the fail stands, as in item 108. Jurors on the hold: "The ring geometry is physically wrong: the rings don't pass in front of the planet's near side, and the planet looks like it's sitting on top of them.", "the polished, self-contained Saturn 'hero shot' composition, a generic illustration that reads more like stock space art than contextual cinematic imagery" and "Saturn's domain-warped FBM cloud swirls with embossed normal-mapped relief along the terminator (plus crisp 1D procedural ringlets with slight pixel aliasing) set against a noticeably softer equirectangular starfield skybox"; on the terrain view: "the real-time shader and alpha-blending artifact where the planet's glowing lit limb meets the semi-transparent inner rings, alongside high-frequency procedural noise and aliasing across the ring bands and cloud textures" and "generic unlabeled CGI beauty shot of Saturn with a flat textured ring disc". The whole film list passes R2 in this round: 19 of 135 votes against 18 of 90 for the controls. Tried: round 34 darkened the cream interior of the inner lanes through the hand over, hid the sky behind the unlit rings after the hold and widened the edge of the globe's shadow on the rings (item 121); round 35 put a tone field on the near lanes of the close picture (item 137). Neither was aimed at the jury, and the soft grooves and the meeting of the rings with the globe (items 39, 40 and 42) are as they were. Nothing follows: the record round scores the frozen build once and is not followed by fixes (kit/08, Phase 6 step 4), so this is open in the delivered build.

Cause as the engineer explains it: the pitch term g = 1 - 0.333 cot(e) of the rise sets both places and no flank number cures it. Cure owed: a new law for the rise, by handover_engineer, as its own commit (mail 432). severe, G13 on 13 of 495 frames: 2434, 2440, 2446, 2447, 2690 to 2692, 2706, 2707, 2710, 2711, 2721 and 2722, worst 2707 at 4.37 percent soft against 2 percent. - Round 1, Phase 2, blockout, whole film. R4 blockout 7, three major, two minor. Next: each stop arrives on its own curve, the approach starts earlier and eases longer, the lookback is reframed with a slow pan. `scorecards/round-001/`.
- Round 2, Phase 2, blockout, whole film. R4 blockout 5, one severe, four major, two minor. Limit reached. After the round: arrivals start off center, the lookback never stops moving, the turn away from Mars is longer. Open items 1 to 5. `scorecards/round-002/`.

- Round 4, Phase 3, mars, look lock round 2 of 5. Started 2026-11-20 UTC on main at 24c2334. Machine checks green before the pack (G1, G2 with 22 tests, G3, G4, G6, G7, G10, G11, G12, G14, G15). The join at the rise cover was severe in round 6 as well, so by the plateau rule the technique changes: ladder "A cover can be seen as a join", rung 1 done on the geometry (one Sun direction for the whole stop, the limb line, the Sun and the ring arcs at the same place on both sides of the swap frame) and rung 2 (a thicker cover that moves with the camera); after the swap one eased pull back on one curve with the Sun, the rings and the stars fixed in the world, and a sky that stays alive to the last frame. (2) Dive, 4142 to 4150: the picture jumps before the cover (the Sun pops in, the ring streaks change sides, the limb flattens and darkens, the Milky Way drops out within eight frames); the swap belongs under the full cover and the approach bends toward the terrain pose before it. (3) Dive, 4118 to 4134: the speed steps up after a near still hold; eased in over thirty frames or more. (4) Stepped copies: at the rise cover's exit the Sun stands as two blobs and the ring arcs as double lines (4413 to 4416, two pictures of the same things at two places), and under the dive cover the bright limb shows through in stacked copies (4159 to 4161); the engine's sample count under a translucent cover is in work on the engine side. (5) Dive cover exit, 4167 to 4170: the Sun goes from absent to full flare and the rings from invisible to crisp within three frames; the clearing is stretched to ten frames or more. (6) Match at 4290: the right ring arc as thick flat white strokes without the approved strands and tint, dark dots along the inner ringlet, the fine inner ringlets fading out before the limb; a thin hard line along the disc's edge inside the cyan glow. Match at 4035: the right moon a quarter too large, both moons with cut out rims, even noise for craters and black night sides without planetshine. (7) Craft, plateau (named in rounds 6 and 21): the cloud deck is smeared into parallel streaks with nothing fine in it (4137, 4290, 4436); ladder "A globe looks plastic, flat or like a web demo", rung 3 (cloud flecks as their own layer with soft shadows) with rung 1 (fine relief). The moon at 4436 is a soft oval. (8) Brandon's order on the terrain view: 4200 to 4379 moves as one plane with weak depth (minor for the critic, first rank here); more forward travel, lower, with a nearer cloud layer. Minors: the hold's turn and drift barely visible; ring strands and Milky Way core softer than approved; the flare streak short; a ring tip like a needle at the horizon; the white rim as an outline over the halo at 4436; stars as dashes right of the rings at 4290. R1 stays 7, R3 rose from 5 to 6, R4 stays 4, R2 passes (0 of 10 against 1 of 10 for the controls), R8 passes. Summary in `scorecards/round-021/`.

- Round 24, Phase 4, sun, round 3 of 3. Started 2026-11-21 18:20 UTC. Judged on main at 530168f. Measures green. R1 9, R2 pass, R3 5, R4 6, R8 pass. 0 severe, 11 major. All four severe issues of round 15 are gone: the kaleidoscope seams behind the sunspot are down to one major, the vertical tile seam in the Milky Way at 247 and the cut through a whiteout at the rise cover are not reported, and the black moat round the glow is down to a minor.
